privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: {app} keeps your photos on your phone. There are no accounts, no ads, and we do not sell or share your data. A few features look things up on public sites, and the app sends anonymous usage numbers that you can turn off.

p: {app} is an iPhone app that finds the games you went to from your own photos and keeps them as a timeline, map and stamp passport. It is provided by {company}. You can reach us at {email}.

Photos: with your permission the app reads your photo library to find games from each photo's date and place. The analysis happens on your phone, including the check that looks for a scoreboard or a stadium in a photo. Your photos are not uploaded and not copied. The app remembers which photos belong to a game by their reference in your library.

Location: if you allow it, the app uses your location while it is open (for example Check in, which finds stadiums near you). Your location is used on your phone to pick nearby stadiums and is not sent to us.

What you enter: games, scores, seats, notes, people you add, favorite teams and your home city are saved in the app's storage on your phone. There is no account and no cloud sync. This data is part of your device backups according to your iOS settings. Deleting the app deletes it.
Calendar: if you tap Add to Calendar, the app asks for permission to add events only. It cannot read your calendar.
Notifications: game-day reminders are scheduled on your phone. Nothing about them is sent to us.

To look up games, the app contacts public sports data sources: ESPN's public schedule service and UEFA's public match feed. A request names a league, a team or a date, such as "the next games for this team". It does not include your name, photos or location. As with any website, the service can see your device's IP address.

The app also downloads team, stadium and schedule data files from a server we run. A request names a data file, such as the games of one league in one season, never a person, a photo or a place you were. The request is not tied to the anonymous identifier used for usage numbers, and we do not keep it beyond the host's ordinary short-lived server logs. Your phone then matches photos to games on the phone itself.
To show the weather at a game, the app sends the stadium's coordinates and the date to Open-Meteo. These are the stadium's coordinates, not yours.
Maps, searching for a city or stadium, satellite pictures of stadiums, and naming your city from your location are done with Apple's map and location services, under Apple's privacy policy.

The app sends anonymous usage events to a server we run, so we can see which features are used and where the app falls short. An event is a short label such as "game added" or "photo scan finished", with simple details such as the sport, a count, or the name of a team whose schedule was looked up. Each event also carries a random identifier created on your phone, the app version, the iOS version, and the country, which our host works out from the connection. The identifier is not linked to your name, email or Apple ID, and a new one is made if you delete and reinstall the app.
These events never include your photos, your location, the names of people you add, your notes or your seat numbers.

You can turn this off at any time with Share anonymous usage in the You tab. We keep these events for up to {retention} months and then delete them. The events are stored with Cloudflare, which hosts our server.
We do not sell your data, share it with advertisers, show ads, or track you across other companies' apps and websites.

You control the photo, location, calendar and notification permissions in iOS Settings, and the app keeps working with fewer features if you say no. You can turn off anonymous usage in the app. Deleting the app removes what it stores on your phone.

Depending on where you live, you may have rights over personal data, such as access or deletion. We do not keep your name or contact details, and usage events cannot be tied to you. If you have a question or a request, write to {email}.
{app} is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them.
Anonymous usage events are sent over an encrypted connection. Everything else stays on your phone.
If we change this policy we will update the date at the top. If a change affects what the app collects, we will tell you in the app.
Questions about privacy: {email}.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.summary: These terms cover your use of {app}. Apple's standard license agreement also applies. The short version: your photos and entries stay yours, game data comes from outside sources and may be wrong, and the app is provided as is.

p: By using {app} you agree to these terms and to Apple's Licensed Application End User License Agreement. If they conflict, Apple's agreement governs the license, and these terms govern the rest. {app} is provided by {company}.
You may use the app on devices you own or control, for your own personal, non-commercial use. You may not copy, modify, reverse engineer or resell it, or use it to build a competing service.
Your photos, notes and entries belong to you. They stay on your phone, and we do not receive them. You give us no rights to them.
Share cards and exported images are made on your phone. What you post, and where, is your choice and your responsibility.

Schedules, scores, weather, venues and other facts in the app come from outside sources and from matching your photos. They can be late, incomplete or wrong. Do not rely on them alone for travel, tickets or anything that matters. Check the official source for your team or league.
Planned games, countdowns and reminders are best effort. iOS may delay or skip a notification.

Team, league and competition names and codes appear only to identify games. They belong to their owners. {app} is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by any team, league, competition or data source.
Do not use the app unlawfully, interfere with its services or the services it contacts, send false data to our servers, or try to get around its limits.
Some features rely on other companies' services, such as Apple's maps and location services and public sports data. Their terms apply to those services, and they may change or stop at any time.
The app is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind, to the extent the law allows. We do not promise that it will be uninterrupted, accurate or error free.

To the extent the law allows, {company} is not liable for indirect, incidental or consequential damages, or for any loss of data or photos, arising from your use of the app. Our total liability for any claim is limited to the amount you paid for the app in the 12 months before the claim, or if you paid nothing, to zero. Some places do not allow these limits, so they may not apply to you.
We may update the app or these terms. If you keep using the app after a change, you accept it. You can stop using the app at any time by deleting it. We may stop providing it.
These terms are governed by the laws of {jurisdiction}, without regard to conflict of law rules, except where your local consumer law says otherwise.
Questions about these terms: {email}.
